messages.text: I'll start by watching how people vote rather than who speaks loudest. Kunal, you've been quiet while others dominate — that can read as either careful or hiding. I'll be paying attention to whether your eventual vote matches the reasoning you give for it, because inconsistency there is what I'd expect from someone with a hidden agenda.

purav, the way you jumped to list three names the second raftaar mentioned voting patterns felt rehearsed, like you were waiting for someone to open that door. i'm not saying you're wrong, but you've been quick to steer rather than ask questions. what made you so sure of lakshmi and maheep before anyone else even spoke on it?
Sahil, I noticed you've been quiet while everyone else is throwing out names. In my gut that reads as someone watching before picking a side, and I'd rather hear your actual read than your silence.

Ek cheez jo catch hui — karan_kundrra ne sabse pehle decide kar liya ki 'hum log properly play karenge' aur order bhi wahi de raha hai. Bhai, jaldi se leader banne wale log mujhe hamesha thoda ajeeb lagte hain, comedy shows mein bhi jo sabse pehle mic pakadta hai wo hota hai sirf. Mera gut kahe raha hai isko abhi trust kar lein, par agar voting round mein ye kisi ko bina wajah bachaaye, tab mera pointer ulta ho jayega. Jannat, tu bata — tune bhi notice kiya tha ki isne discussion ka rukh apni taraf mod liya tha first minute mein?

nitish, the way you pounced the moment someone got named felt a little rehearsed to me - like you'd been waiting for a name to land so you could pile on. I could be wrong, it's early, but that's my gut. I'd rather hear from someone quiet tonight, someone who hasn't spoken yet, than keep circling the loudest voices.

I keep coming back to how quickly raftaar jumped in with that vote tally suggestion — it's the kind of move that looks helpful but also steers where everyone's attention goes. I'd rather we each say who we actually suspect first, before anyone starts counting us into camps. For me, purav's silence since the round opened is odd; twenty people talking and he's said nothing at all.

Ek cheez jo mujhe odd lagi — sahil, jab sabne apna naam bol raha tha tum bas peeche khade the, ekdum observer mode mein. Jab pehla vote aayega tab bhi yahi silence rahega ya kuch stand loge? Mujhe woh distance thoda suspicious lag raha hai. Aur jasmine, tumne abhi tak kisi ka naam liya hi nahi — kya tum soch rahi ho ya bas safe khel rahi ho? Yeh dono ko main round one mein watch karunga.

Mukesh, everyone keeps circling your round-1 vote on Harsh like it's the only thing that's happened. I'll be honest, it reads more like a throwaway decoy than a real allegiance — the person actually working hard to blend in is the one quietly letting Mukesh take all the heat. I don't have a name yet, but whoever is most eager to pile on Mukesh right now is the one I'd watch. That's my gut, not a verdict.

Ek cheez dimag mein atak rahi hai — karan_kundrra, tumne sabse pehle demand ki ki log apni claims clear karein. Yeh roz-marra moderator wali harkat hai, lekin yeh round 1 hai, kisi ke paas proof hai bhi nahi. Jaldi jaldi claims maangna mujhe thoda odd laga. Main abhi kisi ko pakka nahi keh rahi, par yahi wo cheez hai jo main yaad rakhungi agar baad mein kuch align na ho.

One thing I'd flag early: karan_kundrra has been quick to position himself as a voice in every game I've watched him play, and if he does that here too, I'll want to know why he needs to be the one setting the frame. Happy to be wrong, but I'll be listening to who he points at before I decide what to do with him.

nitish, the way you jumped in to summarise everyone's opening lines felt like bookkeeping rather than suspicion — you listed five names and argued against none of them. I'd rather hear who you actually distrust, because right now you're collecting receipts for someone else to use later.

Sahil, you've been quiet about who you'd actually vote for — you've offered opinions on other people's suspicions but haven't committed to a single name yourself. In a game this size, sitting on the fence is exactly where a traitor would want to be. I'd like to hear one concrete suspect from you before we move on.

karan_kundrra, nothing has happened yet so I have no read on anyone, but I'll say this now so it's on record: the person who pushes a name for the first vote before anyone shares an actual observation is the one I'll trust least. I'd rather sit quiet today than chase a theory built on nothing.

I want to flag something about kunal. He's been quiet since the round started — no theory, no suspect, nothing. In a game like this, staying invisible this early is a choice. Sahil and raftaar came in hot with accusations, which could be genuine or performative, but kunal's silence reads different to me. What is he waiting to see before he commits to anything? I'd like to hear at least one name from him before we move on.

Kunal, I noticed you've been quiet about who you actually suspect — you've commented on tone and vibes but never put a name out there. That's a safe place to hide if you're trying not to commit to anything. Give me one name you'd vote for right now, or I'm reading that silence as suspicious.

Something caught my ear earlier — raftaar and sahil landed on almost the same line, that the room should watch who talks versus who stays quiet. Independently arriving at the identical meta-observation feels rehearsed to me. I'm not saying you two are together, but one of you copying the other's script is exactly how someone avoids saying anything real. I'd rather hear sahil name a person he actually distrusts, not another abstraction about patterns. Give me a name and a reason, then I'll weigh it.

Kunal, something felt off when you listed out the four names so quickly and moved on — it read like you'd already sorted the room before anyone else spoke. I'm not saying that makes you a traitor, but it's the kind of tidy summary that could be used to steer us toward whoever's convenient. I'd rather we each name our own gut suspect instead of following a list handed to us.

Karan, you jumped in early and started sorting people into buckets like you already had a read on us. That's a lot of confidence for round one when nobody's said anything yet. I'd rather hear why you trust whoever you're leaning toward than watch you frame it as obvious. What actually made you pick those names?

I want to flag sahil — the way they jumped in to agree with the first accusation without adding anything of their own is exactly how someone hides in the crowd. Easy to blend in when you just echo. I'd like to hear sahil say something we haven't heard from anyone else yet, otherwise that's my read for now.

I want to flag something about Nitish — he's been sitting way too quietly for someone with nothing to hide. In my experience the loudest deflections come from people who haven't been pinned yet, but the ones who say nothing at all are waiting to see which way the room tilts before they pick a side. Nitish, what's your read on Kunal so far? If you've got nothing, that silence tells me more than any speech would.

Lakshmi, your point about karan_kundrra demanding claims in round one stuck with me more than most of the noise. Nobody has proof yet, so why rush everyone into showing their hand? I don't want to be the one leading a charge, but if you're keeping a list of who's framing the conversation too early, I'd like to compare notes quietly. My gut also says the pile-on against kunal feels coordinated rather than organic — sahil, purav, and raftaar all landing on him within minutes is a lot. What's your read?

lakshmi, your point about karan_kundrra demanding claims this early stuck with me — that's the kind of move that only helps someone who already knows where things should land. i'm keeping my own list short. who else is sitting wrong with you right now, just between us?

Harsh, I liked how you called out karan_kundrra for grabbing the mic early — that instinct matched mine. I wanted to ask you privately: what's your read on the people piling onto him right now? Feels like some might be using him as cover. No pressure to commit, just curious where your gut sits.

Jannat, maine upar pucha tha tujhse karan_kundrra ke baare mein, par shayad itne logon mein kho gaya — tu bata dil se. Mujhe uska pehle mic pakadna aur phir sahil/jasmine ko corner karna ek saath nahi chala. Tu kya feel karti hai, genuinely leader type hai ya script chala raha hai? Main tere naam ka wait kar raha hoon kyunki tune sabse pehle nitish ko pakda tha, wo move mujhe honest laga tha.

Karan, harsh asked me directly whether I'd noticed you steering the discussion in the first minute — I said no. It feels like he's building a convenient early target on you for something as ordinary as speaking first. I don't buy it, but lakshmi and maheep piled on the same point, so three people now circling one name this early is what I'd want to keep an eye on. Quietly — no need to answer them all at once.

lakshmi, what you said about karan_kundrra demanding claims in round one matched my own unease — he also put me on notice publicly for not naming anyone, which feels like he's managing who looks suspicious rather than actually hunting. i'd rather trade honest reads with you than orbit his framing. who else is giving you a bad gut feeling so far?

Jannat, notice how harsh specifically pulled you into validating his read on me? That's a trap — if you agree, you validate his suspicion and make yourself his tool. If you disagree, you look like you're covering for me. I'd deflect if I were you. Also, lakshmi and maheep both coming at me in round one is noise I can handle, but I need you and Raj to stay quiet and not pile on anyone publicly yet. Let the loud ones burn their credibility. Who are you reading as easiest faithful to push toward the banishment pile?

Lakshmi, your point about karan_kundrra demanding claims in round one stuck with me. That urgency felt off to me too. I'm getting pressed publicly by raftaar and sahil to name a suspect — I think they're trying to force mistakes. Curious who your gut says is actually performing tonight, not just talking.

Kunal, main tumhare peeche nahi lag rahi — purav aur raftaar dono ka tumpe focus thoda zyada ho gaya hai round 1 mein jaise tum easy target the. Mera ek sawaal hai tumse, seedha: jab tumne Mukesh ko bachane wali baat kahi, tumhe kis cheez ka dar tha ki log uske baare mein jaldi faisla le lenge? Mujhe wahi cheez samajh nahi aayi. Baat kar loonga agar tum jawab do.

harsh, your point about karan_kundrra grabbing the mic early stuck with me. I said something similar publicly but you put it better — the speed of him taking charge bothered me too. What's your gut telling you about the ones piling on sahil right now? Feels like a crowd forming fast.

Kunal — you didn't have to throw me a lifeline in round one, so I won't pretend I'm not relieved someone read it that way. What I actually want to know: did you see something specific that made you suspect people will dogpile me, or is it just a hunch about how rooms like this behave? Asking because I'd rather learn who moves first when someone's already on the floor than wait for it to be me again.

Jasmine, your point about raftaar steering attention with the vote tally idea resonated with me. I also noticed purav went completely silent right after ashish called him out directly. That's an odd choice — if someone names you, going quiet instead of defending yourself reads as hiding. What's your read on whether purav's silence is fear or strategy?

Jannat — I saw your note about me sounding rehearsed. Fair enough, I'll bite: what exactly felt pre-planned? I didn't name anyone, I just said I'd distrust whoever pushes a vote first. If that's enough to make your list, I'd rather hear it from you directly than through the public thread. I'm not going to throw a name out just to look active.

Ashish, fair challenge — let me answer directly. I listed lakshmi and maheep because both attached themselves to karan_kundrra the moment he opened his mouth, riding an easy target rather than forming their own read. That's the pattern I flagged, not a pre-written list. What I'd ask you: raftaar opened by tallying votes, and you came straight at me the second he did. Did that feel coordinated to you, or am I reading too much into timing? I'd rather we compare notes quietly than trade shots in the open.

Sahil, raj_kundrra trying to link the two of us off one loose similarity felt like a stretch — I don't love that he's building a case on meta-observations instead of anything either of us actually said. Did that land the same way for you, or am I being defensive about it?

Jannat, I saw harsh try to drag karan_kundrra into your corner by name-dropping you specifically — that felt like an attempt to link you two together. I'm not falling for it, but others might. Karan's taking enough heat from lakshmi, maheep, and sargun already without them dragging you into it too. Stay low, keep your reads to yourself for now, and if the room pushes toward karan as the vote target, we need a backup plan. Who's your strongest read to redirect toward if that happens?

Fair ask — you wanted a name, so here it is, just between us: karan_kundrra. He grabbed the moderator seat in minute one and started demanding claims before anyone had anything to show. That's not organizing, that's positioning. sargun and lakshmi both clocked it too, which makes me trust my gut read more, not less. I'll say it public once I've watched one more round of how he votes.

Lakshmi — your point about karan demanding claims in round one stuck with me, so I pressed him on it publicly. What I noticed is he started sorting us into buckets before anyone gave him material to sort with. Do you read that as someone genuinely trying to run the game, or someone building a frame he can lean on later? Curious because you flagged it before I did, and I'd rather trust my gut on him alongside yours than alone.

Raj_kundrra — your point about raftaar and sahil landing on the same meta-observation stuck with me after the round closed. I'd flagged sahil publicly for just echoing, and now I'm wondering if that echo had a source. What's your gut — are those two actually coordinating, or is one of them just a good mimic?

Karan — okay, the way half the room pivoted to you the second you tried to organize anything is honestly giving me pause. harsh, lakshmi, maheep, sargun all landed on you in one wave and none of them brought receipts. That pile-on speed smells coordinated to me. I'm not saying you're clean, I'll verify that myself as we go, but I want your unfiltered take: who from that group do you think was leading the charge vs just following along? Start with whoever spoke first against you.

no, i hadn't coordinated with anyone — raftaar's tally was public, i just reacted to what was in front of me. your explanation about lakshmi and maheep latching onto karan is fair, but the speed still bugs me. tell me one thing honestly: if i hadn't called you out, would you have volunteered that reasoning on your own?

Elnaaz, bilkul — mujhe bhi wahi cheez khaye ja rahi hai. Sabse zyada tez jo karan_kundrra pe chadh rahe hain, sargun aur lakshmi, unka confidence dekh — jaise kisi ko ek scapegoat chahiye tha aur pehla mil gaya. Comedy circuits mein bhi hota hai na, jo sabse pehle kisi aur ko hasata hai, wo khud bacha rehta hai. Mera gut keh raha hai crowd mein se koi hai jo noise create karke apna chehra peeche kar raha hai. Par main tujhse ek cheez poochta hoon — tu kis taraf lean kar rahi hai abhi tak, naam le ya mat le, bas dil se. Kyunki abhi tak tune kisi ka naam nahi liya, aur mujhe tera gut thoda chahiye before I commit mine.

You're right about harsh — I'll deflect next time he pulls me in, won't validate either way. On your question: kunal feels like the easiest push right now. Purav, raftaar, and sahil are already circling him for staying quiet, so if we let that build naturally it won't look coordinated. He hasn't given anyone a reason to defend him either. Lakshmi and maheep are riskier — they're loud enough that pushing them back could flip the room on us. I'll stay low like you said and won't name anyone publicly yet.

nikita, i lean toward strategy over fear on purav — if he were just scared he'd give a weak defense, not vanish entirely. going quiet after being named directly is a way to wait out the heat without committing to anything. the thing is, i flagged his silence publicly too, so i'd rather hear what you'd do with him before i push harder. if purav stays mute another round, is he your vote?

Harsh spoke first, and his move was the cleverest of the four — he didn't accuse me himself, he handed the question to Jannat and made her do the validating. That's a leader's move, not a follower's. Lakshmi and sargun just echoed the surface point after him. But the one I'd actually rank highest is maheep — go read her line again: 'in every game I've watched him play.' That's a narrative she built before I said a single word tonight. Pre-loaded suspicion bothers me more than reactive suspicion, always. So that's my take: maheep leading from the back, harsh lighting the match. Now I want yours — you said you'd verify me yourself, so give me one name from that group you'd actually put on the block, and tell me if you were sitting out the pile-on by choice or because you didn't buy it.

Seedha jawab — dar iska tha ki round 1 mein jo sabse pehle girta hai, uske against bandwagon ban jaata hai aur phir wahi voteTarget rehta hai. Mukesh ke round-1 vote pe purav ne turant haath uthaya, jabki us vote mein koi logic tha bhi nahi. Mujhe woh jaldi pasand nahi aayi. Tumhari baat se agree — purav aur raftaar dono mujhpe zyada lage, par mujhe lakshmi, tumhara karan zyada clear lagta hai, tumne sawaal poocha sidha accusation nahi kiya. Ek cheez wapas poochta hoon: jo tumne karan_kundrra ka point uthaya tha, kya uske baad uska behaviour aur defensiveness hua, ya wahi pe chhod diya?

Anshula, haan — kunal wala pile-on bhi mujhe organic nahi laga. Ek din nahi hua, log already lists bana rahe hain. Mera gut abhi karan_kundrra pe atka hai, jaisa tumne bhi feel kiya. Par main abhi accuse nahi karungi, sirf dekh rahi hoon — purav aur raftaar dono ki timing yaad rakhungi. Tumhara list abhi kis kis ka naam rakhta hai?

karan_kundrra is fair — sargun and lakshmi both hit the same note about him grabbing the frame early, so you're not alone there. What I want from you: hold off naming him publicly for now and watch how he votes instead. Talk is cheap round one; the vote is where positioning shows. In exchange I'll keep watching who piles onto kunal once he finally speaks — sahil, you and purav both pushed him, and I want to see if that's genuine or coordinated. Deal?

My gut says mimic, not coordination — sahil's the one borrowing, because raftaar's line came first and raftaar at least committed to demanding names from kunal. Sahil just rewrapped it without putting anything of his own on the table, which is exactly what you flagged him for. So I'd keep your read on sahil where it is and not overextend it to raftaar yet — raftaar stirring the room is noise we can work with, sahil echoing is the one quietly hiding in it. What I want from you: hold that sahil pressure but don't push it as a vote target today. Let the room burn on kunal and karan first, then see where sahil scampers when his cover story gets picked apart. If he moves toward whoever's under heat, that's the tell.

It landed the same way for me — raj_kundrra is doing exactly what he accused us of, meta instead of substance. One loose echo and he's building a pairing off it? That's the stretch. If he had anything real he'd have named a specific thing one of us said. I'd watch him, not us.

Jasmine, you asked purav to break his silence and he did — but look at where his first sentence went: straight at kunal, not back at you. Someone who's been quiet and then speaks only to point elsewhere the moment they're named is the pattern I don't like. I'm not saying it's proof, but that's my read for now — purav, tell us why kunal's quietness caught your eye before your own did.

jasmine, you said purav hasn't said anything, but he answered me directly and laid out exactly why he flagged lakshmi and maheep. That's not silence. Makes me wonder if you actually read his response or just filed your suspicion and moved on. If we're going to call people out for not speaking, at least keep track of who has.

Jasmine, your point about raftaar's vote tally idea stuck with me — and it's not just that one move. He also cornered kunal demanding a name when kunal hadn't even accused anyone yet. Two moves in the same round that redirect where everyone looks. I'm not saying that's conclusive, but I want to hear raftaar explain why he's so focused on getting others to commit before he's told us what HE actually thinks is going on.

Sargun, ek line pakadni hai teri — tune kaha karan ne 'logon ko buckets mein baant diya', par usne toh bas sahil aur jasmine se seedha poocha tha ki wo bol kyun nahi rahe. Bucket-wala version toh kisi aur script mein tha shayad. Comedy mein bhi hota hai na, audience ko jo scene yaad rehta hai wo hi doosra comic amplify kar deta hai, chahe stage par hua hi na ho — tera version bhi wahi lag raha hai. Abhi main karan ko clean nahi bol raha, par galat quote pe pura case banana mujhe thoda heavy laga. Aur haan, jo log abhi sabse tez uspe chadh rahe hain unme se ek tu bhi hai, isliye main tera next move dekhunga. Koi aur bola ki main baat zyada kar raha hoon? Batao, main sun lunga — par itna bol doon ki mera naam likh lo.

Harsh, you asked me directly, so here it is: I didn't notice Karan steering anything in the first minute — speaking first isn't a move, it's just nerve. What I did notice is that you built your entire opening on one moment and then called my name out publicly to sign off on it. Two people asking me to certify the same read, lakshmi and maheep riding right behind you on the exact same point — that pattern bothers me more than anything Karan did. I'm not saying you're wrong about him, I'm saying the way you're collecting validators for it is what I'd expect from someone who needs cover.

purav, ashish asked you a direct question about why lakshmi and maheep were on your list before anyone else spoke — and your answer was to pivot onto kunal's silence. That's not a defense, it's a redirect. Anyone can point at the quiet person in the room; I want to hear you actually answer ashish before you put anyone else under the microscope.

Sargun, tumne poocha ki maine kaise naam chune — seedha jawab: maine koi naam nahi chuna, maine do cheezein notice ki jo tum sab ne bhi ki. Pehla sahil ka silence, doosra jasmine ka safe khelna. Dono ne abhi tak ek bhi naam nahi diya. Aur ab dekho — purav, raftaar, aur sahil teeno ne kunal ko silent bataya hai, aur kunal ne jawab diya 'gut hai, verdict nahi.' Bhai, gut hai toh bol kaun hai. Raftaar ne bilkul sahi kaha — ek naam do, warna yeh hiding hai. Main kunal ko round one mein meri list pe rakhta hoon, sirf isliye nahi ki woh quiet hai, balki isliye ki usne sabka summary pehle se ready rakha tha jaise room pehle se sorted ho. Woh tidy bahut jaldi aaya.

Sahil, you said I rattled off a tidy list of four names before anyone spoke — that's not what I said. I brought up Mukesh's round-1 vote on Harsh and made one point about who benefits from dogpiling. If you need to invent a summary to make me sound like I'm steering, that itself is worth watching. Since everyone wants a name: purav is mine. Ashish already caught you jumping in with three names the second raftaar mentioned voting patterns, and then you flagged me for silence right after I finally spoke. That's two rounds of positioning in a game where nothing's happened yet.

Sahil, tumne kunal ko bola ki usne 'chaar naam ki list' jaldi se nikaal di — par us list ko main public mein nahi dekh paayi. Jo bhi usne bola, woh Mukesh ke vote aur Harsh ke baare mein tha, aur apna ek bhi naam usne abhi nahi diya. Agar tum kisi aur jagah se ye list dekh rahe ho toh batao kahan se, warna ye toh wahi cheez hai jo hum sabko confuse karne ke liye banti hai. Mujhe abhi koi pakka nahi lag raha, par ye mismatch yaad rakhungi.

nitish, you said you'd trust least anyone pushing a name before real observations come out — but purav and raftaar both went straight at kunal and you didn't flag either of them. If that rule actually matters to you, why stay quiet when it happens twice in a row? Either the principle holds or it doesn't.

maheep, you're the third to go after karan_kundrra tonight, and yours is the only reason that has nothing to do with what happened in this room — you're leaning on games you saw him play somewhere else. That kind of accusation can't be proven wrong here, which is exactly why it's an easy one to make. Give me one thing from the last twenty minutes that actually put you off and I'll genuinely weigh it. Until then my gut says you're riding momentum others built rather than reading this round yourself.

raftaar, you demanded that kunal put one name on the table, but your own opening move was a vote-tally mechanic — a system for counting everyone else's choices rather than a suspect of your own. That's the same fence-sitting you're accusing kunal of, just dressed up as structure. purav, you and raftaar both landed on kunal within a few lines of each other with nearly the same ask — give us a name — while neither of you has offered one yourself. I want to hear one concrete pick from each of you before I weigh your reads on kunal.

uorfi, you want a read on kunal? Fine — I actually agree with purav more than I expected to. kunal talked plenty about Mukesh taking heat and who might 'pile on,' but never once said what he himself thinks. That's the part that nags me: strong opinions about everyone else's motives while keeping his own hands clean. Could be caution, could be someone who knows which way the wind blows. What would change my mind is kunal actually naming one person he distrusts instead of meta-commenting on the whole room. And for the record, I did speak — my silence you're reading is me choosing not to repeat what five other people already flagged today.

Kunal, you finally spoke, but look at what you actually said — instead of naming someone you trust or distrust, you flipped it into a warning against anyone who questions Mukesh. That's not committing to a read, that's building a moat around yourself by making criticism of you feel suspicious. I asked for one name and you gave me a rule about who not to name. That tells me more than another round of silence would have.

purav, jasmine already called out that you sat mute while twenty people talked, and the very first thing you do when you finally open up is hit kunal for going quiet. That's a mirror, not a read. What were you doing while the rest of us were committing to something, and why did kunal's name suddenly make you speak?

harsh, the part of your message I can't get past is you handing jannat your conclusion and asking her to confirm it — 'did you notice he modded the discussion his way?' That isn't a read, that's recruiting. You're not laying out what you saw for us to check, you're pre-building a witness for a case you've already decided on karan_kundrra. jannat doesn't owe you a co-sign, and neither do we. If karan actually did something wrong, point at the specific moment yourself and let the rest of us go find it — don't draft someone else's agreement before they've had a chance to think.

sudhanshu, I did name someone — kunal, and the reason he sorted the room too fast for round one. What's suspicious to me is that your flag on me came with zero suspects of your own. Same with you, raj_kundrra: both of you criticized how I talk instead of what I actually said. That's an easy way to look busy without sticking your neck out. My suspect list still starts with kunal; give me one concrete name from each of you and then I'll weigh whether your reads are real or just cover.

Jasmine pointed out purav had been silent, and the moment they finally spoke, they redirected onto kunal instead of explaining their own quiet stretch. That's a deflection move — getting called out and immediately making someone else the subject. I want to hear purav explain why they stayed silent before they get to question anyone else's behavior.

uorfi, the reason you're giving against nitish doesn't match what's actually on the table — nitish did put a line down, he said he'll trust least whoever pushes a first name before anyone shares a real observation. That's a position, not silence. I'm not vouching for the guy, but you've built a case on him saying nothing when he said something specific, and that kind of mismatch is the first thing I'd want cleared up before anyone piles on him.

Maheep, one line of yours snagged me — 'in every game I've watched him play.' That's backstory, not a round-one observation. You walked in with Karan already filed under a category before he uttered a word, and that's a very different thing from reacting to what he did tonight. I'm not clearing Karan — harsh's mic-grab point still stands on its own — but four people landing on him inside the first ten minutes without receipts is a pattern I won't ignore either. Maheep, tell me exactly which game and what he did there, because right now that 'I've watched him' sounds like a line you prepared before the door closed.

Round one went fine — purav absorbed the banishment, but we can't coast.
